about.metaDescription: Who writes this journal, how it is built, and where to find me.
about.heading: About
about.intro: My name is Thomas Caron, and I write this journal — the stories as well as the code. It is a personal project run like a real one: tickets, architecture decisions written down and dated, and tests that guard what breaks in silence. If you are here to judge work rather than to read a trip, everything is open: the code, and the reasoning that goes with it, filed next to the code it explains.
about.madeIntro: There is no database. Every trip is a file versioned in the repository, and publishing means committing. The whole site is computed at build time: a visitor receives HTML, CSS, and the strict minimum of JavaScript.
about.choicePrerender: Every page is prerendered at build time; none is computed on demand. A test reads the manifest the build produces to prove it — that invariant breaks in silence, with a build that exits successfully.
about.choiceMap: The world map is SVG projected at build time by d3-geo: zero bytes of map library on the client, with one trip as with sixty.
about.choiceBudget: Weight is a budget, not an intention: 150 KB brotli of initial JavaScript per page, 34 KB for the world's outlines. Two tests weigh the build's real bytes every time and refuse to let an overrun through.
about.choiceBoundaries: The boundaries between the layers are ESLint rules — and other tests check that those rules really refuse something, because a rule that no longer guards anything looks exactly like a rule that does.
about.choiceAdr: Architecture decisions are written down and dated, with the alternatives weighed, what they cost, and what would invalidate them.
about.stack: Next.js 16 on the App Router and React 19, in strict TypeScript. next-intl for localised routing, d3-geo and TopoJSON for the projection, Zod to validate the content, plain CSS with custom properties. Vitest, Playwright and axe for the tests. Deployed on Vercel.
about.stackAbsent: No Tailwind, no state manager, no HTTP client, no icon library. Every absent dependency is a decision, and the budget above is what defends it.

purpose.heading: What this journal is after
purpose.body: I travel, and I write down what I keep of it: the stops in the order they happened, the dates, the photographs, and what a place did to me. Not a guide, not a ranking — a journal, kept so that a trip can be read whole rather than in fragments.
purpose.method: It is also a project run like a real one: decisions written down and dated, tests that guard what breaks in silence, and a map drawn at build time rather than loaded in the browser. The code is open, and the reasoning is filed next to it.
